reader.requirement: In SPECIAL-NAMES, no literal of the ALPHABET clause literal phrase (literal-1, literal-2 after THROUGH, literal-3 after ALSO) and no literal of the CLASS clause (literal-4, literal-5 after THROUGH) may be a symbolic-character figurative constant (a name declared by SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS, before or after the clause, alone or as ALL symbolic-character); other figurative constants and literals stay legal.

reader.notes: Every literal slot refuses a symbolic-character name, declared before or after the clause. One diagnostic-quality lead: CLASS C IS "X" SYM-A THRU "C" is refused by the parser (COBOL1970, 'not a clause of the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph') instead of the SR5 screen, at 85 and 2023; no legal 1985 source puts a word there, so the 1985 rule is unharmed, but at 2023 a constant-name in that position may be rejected (not probed). Messages cite §2023:12.3.7.3 SR11.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.4.5.2-4.5.3: at 85 the clause order is ALPHABET, SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS, CLASS, so a symbolic-character in an ALPHABET literal can only be a forward reference (covered by the reader's snl1t/snl2/snl3), and a contained program has no Configuration Section (§1985:VI.4.2), so no inherited case exists. Run at --std 85: CLASS literal-4 alone (s5cls1) COBOL1671; literal-4 opening a THRU range (s6cls4t) COBOL1671; ALL symbolic in CLASS (s2clsall) COBOL1671; symbolic declared IN alphabet-name-2 then used in an ALPHABET (s1in) COBOL1906 (plus COBOL2987 for the out-of-order clause); symbolic declared after CLASS (s3cls4) refused (COBOL2987/COBOL1970). Other figurative constants stay legal: ALPHABET "A" ALSO QUOTE "B" THRU "D" HIGH-VALUE with CLASS ... SPACE (s4fig) compiles and runs (IN).
